title: Strings from font data must be cleaned before they become OS identifiers
rule: Before a name from a font's name table (PostScript name, family) becomes part of an OS identifier (a registry value name, a file or symlink name, a CoreText or fontconfig key), strip control characters, U+0000 included, and fall back to the file stem when nothing is left. In the Win32 or C string wrapper, refuse an interior NUL with InvalidInput instead of passing a pointer the OS will cut short. Add a test that activates faces whose names contain a NUL (at the end, in the middle, only control characters) and asserts the returned handles equal what list_active reports.
rationale: E6.3 (#76): a malformed PostScript name with a NUL made the HKCU value name differ from the returned handle (Win32 stops at NUL), could exhaust the suffix search, and a leading NUL wrote the (Default) value of the Fonts key.
